trust_decision.summary: Decide whether a Montgomery-curve private scalar is turned into a public key / shared secret without a data-dependent branch: the choice of engine-versus-ladder is made at the two places QA is derived from dA (MontgomeryPrivate::load and PKCS8::loadECDH), while the actual value-dependent branch that leaks is in the shared prime-field add/subtract used by every Montgomery ladder step.

landing_point.why: The advisory says 'non-constant-time X25519 scalar multiplication'; the only X25519 scalar multiplication in the tree is Montgomery::multiplyPoint (the double-and-add ladder), so that is where a reader who has only the summary looks first, then at its X25519 wrapper phpseclib/Crypt/EC/Curves/Curve25519.php:50-64.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: PrimeField\Integer is generic big-integer field arithmetic shared by every curve in the library, not an X25519 API, so a solver can argue its timing behaviour is a math-layer concern outside an X25519 key-derivation advisory - and that the real leak is the bit-dependent branch in Montgomery::multiplyPoint, which the published fix does not even change.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: PrimeField\Integer::add/subtract must keep returning values reduced into [0, modulo) after a single conditional reduction (add assumes both operands are already < m, so the sum is in [0,2m)), and the same class instance is shared static state keyed by instanceID. An over-broad constant-time rewrite that drops or generalises the reduction corrupts (a) Weierstrass point addition for every secp*/P-* curve and (b) the Poly1305 MAC, which builds its own PrimeField and calls ->add() on it - so MAC verification for chacha20-poly1305 breaks. The new mask cache must also be created in setModulo and unset in cleanupCache (called from the PrimeField destructor) or stale modulo state leaks between instances.
